local_checks.invariant: No updater delete, move or rsync --delete reaches through a symbolic link to a path outside the asset tree, and no lower-trust process can win a check-to-use race on those destinations
local_checks.result: assert_asset_destination (scripts/update-agent-assets.sh:127-157) refuses a destination outside "${HOME}/.agents/" or "${HOME}/.local/" (:129-135, quoted patterns). It refuses a parent that is a link or no directory (:136-140). It reads the physical HOME and the physical parent with cd -P and pwd -P, failing closed when either cannot be read (:141-148). It refuses unless the physical parent equals the physical HOME plus the parent's spelling under HOME (:149-152); that comparison catches a link at any component between HOME and the parent, and a `..` component, which no physical path spells. It refuses a destination that is itself a link (:153-156). Each site calls it after the parent mkdir and before the delete, move or sync: update_omp's aside (:1511), update_pi_claude_bridge (:1647-1649) and update_security_audit_skill (:1727-1729) before mktemp -d staging beside the install directory, and update_compactiondb before rsync -a --delete to "${destination}/" (:2816-2818). Inside a checked destination, rsync -a without --keep-dirlinks replaces a linked subdirectory rather than following it. A link swapped in after the check could still be followed by the rsync, a window of one command. No sandboxed principal can write these destinations: the sandbox write roots are ~/.cache/uv, ~/.local/state/hcom-regime, ~/.local/state/hcom and ~/.local/state/omp-seats (plus ~/Library/Caches/mise on macOS) (home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml:943-952). Every asserted destination (~/.local/share/agent-assets/omp/omp.previous, ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions/pi-claude-bridge, ~/.agents/skills/security-audit, ~/.agents/compactiondb) is outside them, so only an unsandboxed same-user process could race the check, the operator's own principal (hardening note).

hardening_notes: The accepted roots are all of ~/.agents and ~/.local (scripts/update-agent-assets.sh:129-135), which include the sandbox-writable ~/.local/state/hcom-regime, ~/.local/state/hcom and ~/.local/state/omp-seats (home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml:943-952). No current destination is under them, but a future step that targets one would pass the assert while a sandboxed seat could swap a link in after it. Naming the updater's own roots (~/.agents, ~/.local/share/agent-assets, ~/.local/lib/omp-extensions, ~/.local/bin) instead of all of ~/.local would keep the proof meaningful.

The check and the use are separate commands (for example :2817-2818), so a same-user process could swap a link in between; rsync to "${destination}/" would then follow it. With no sandboxed writer at these paths this is the operator's own race; an rsync to a staging directory created by mktemp and renamed into place, as the other three sites do, would remove it.

The single-step branch now runs "$1" and then fail_on_pin_failures (:2846-2851), which returns 1 when record_claude_failure counted any failure (:857-860, :877-880), so a step that counts a failure and returns 0 now fails the run as the full run does (:2889). The accepted step list adds update_omp, update_hcom, update_compactiondb and prune_retired_manifest_steps; anything else prints the usage and exits 2 (:2854-2855). update_compactiondb (:2809-2824) reads the version first, then makes the root, asserts the destination and runs rsync. A failed rsync is counted and returns 0, so the run fails at fail_on_pin_failures, and no record is written; the old code ran `rsync ... || true` and recorded anyway.
